first_impression.reaction: Typed 'honeymoon planner cost' on the train. First line: it depends. Second line: 'A number on its own tells you very little.' Okay, fair, but I wanted a number. Kept going only because Key Takeaways was right there and short. The takeaways are clear but they tell me what to ask, not how planners actually charge. That bit (flat fee, percentage, commissions or a mix) is hiding in the FAQ at the bottom. Once I found it, it was a straight answer. Not a bad page, just makes me scroll for the useful line.

journey.quote: A number on its own tells you very little.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it costs. I get that it varies, but this is the first thing I see and it's basically 'it depends'. Honest, not satisfying.

journey.quote: The planner's fee and the cost of the trip itself are two separate things, so ask about each on its own terms.
journey.reaction: Actually useful. I hadn't split those two in my head. Good first bullet.

journey.quote: Ask any planner how they charge and whether they receive commissions from suppliers, and get the answer in writing.
journey.reaction: How DO they charge though? The ways planners charge are listed further down, not here. This is where I'd want them.

journey.quote: With Wedded Wonderland, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Tells me when the fee gets agreed, not what it is or how it's worked out. Fine for a takeaway, but it doesn't move me.

journey.quote: Ask whether it is a flat fee, a percentage of the trip, supplier commissions or a mix, what it covers and when it is payable, and get all of it in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: There it is. This is the closest thing to an answer to my search, and it's in the last section. Should be in the first 100 words.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: Do you receive commissions from the suppliers you book, and will you tell us which?
journey.reaction: Good list. Short, plain, I'd screenshot this and send it to my fiance before we talk to anyone.

journey.section: Paying in Australian dollars or another currency
journey.quote: Money transfer services in Australia must be registered with AUSTRAC, so check that before you use one.
journey.reaction: Now we're on transfer services and Australian regulators. Drifting a long way from what a planner costs, and it's clearly written for Australians. Scrolled past.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, a few steps protect the money you put into a honeymoon.
journey.reaction: Dated, nice. At least I know this is current.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.
journey.reaction: Tapped this heading hoping for how their fee works. It's how the process works: you'll be told the fee later, in writing. Heading promises more than the section gives.

unanswered_questions: What does a honeymoon planner typically charge, even as a rough range? (deferred business detail: page deliberately gives no figures)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage of the trip, or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions from the suppliers it books? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real honeymoon you've planned, with the fee and trip cost shown separately? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras for booking through you? (deferred business detail)
Do you work with couples who live outside Australia, and can you quote in another currency? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: A number on its own tells you very little.
turn_offs_found.why: I searched for a cost and the opening tells me there isn't one. I understand why, but the useful part (the ways planners charge) should follow straight after instead of sitting in the FAQ.

turn_offs_found.quote: How much does a honeymoon planner cost?
turn_offs_found.why: The heading that exactly matches my search is the first FAQ, at the very bottom of a long page. On a phone that's a lot of scrolling for the line I came for.

turn_offs_found.quote: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
turn_offs_found.why: Heading doesn't match what's underneath. It describes the steps to get started, not how the fee works.

would_share_with: My fiance, the 'How planners may charge, as questions to ask' list, as a checklist for any planner we talk to

cta_reaction.quote: To start that conversation, [enquire about Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planner-cost&utm_content=secondary).
cta_reaction.why: I don't know this brand, I came for a quick answer, and everything here is in Australian dollars and Australian rules. I might bookmark the page for the questions list. I'm not enquiring from a train after one read.

top_3_changes: Put the ways planners charge in the first 100 words or Key Takeaways: lift 'a flat fee, a percentage of the trip, supplier commissions or a mix' from the FAQ into the intro or the second takeaway, so 'Ask any planner how they charge' comes with the options. Generic reader advice, no Wedded Wonderland figures needed.

Rename 'How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland' to match its content (for example 'Agreeing your fee with Wedded Wonderland'), since the section covers the process and written agreement, not how the fee is calculated.

Tighten the off-question sections for phone readers: 'Paying in Australian dollars or another currency' and 'Protecting what you pay' could become a short checklist, and the intro could say once that the guide is written for Australian couples.

VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Should the intro state the Australian audience explicitly, given the page relies on ACCC, AUSTRAC and AUD throughout?

assumptions: Priya arrived from a Google search for 'honeymoon planner cost' on her phone, does not know the brand and is not based in Australia, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood is 1.
Deferred business details (fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, perks) are not penalised; the deliberate absence of figures is noted as a reaction only.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, Key Takeaways, the FAQ, the questions list, a skim of the currency and protection sections and the Wedded Wonderland section.
